references.text: The next verse continues the contrast: [ref:Luk 12:48|Luke 12:48] describes the servant who did not know his master's will and is therefore to be beaten with fewer blows – the principle that to whom much is given, much is required.
[ref:Jak 4:17|James 4:17] states the same principle: "The one who knows what good he ought to do but does not do it, for him it is sin." Knowledge of what is right brings responsibility.

[ref:4 Mos 15:30-31|Numbers 15:30–31] distinguishes between sins committed intentionally ("with a high hand") and those done in ignorance – the one who sins knowingly shall be cut off because he has despised the Lord's word.

[ref:5 Mos 25:2-3|Deuteronomy 25:2–3] contains the law that a guilty person is to be beaten with a number of blows corresponding to his offense – the image Jesus uses of the servant who "shall receive many blows" (δαρήσεται πολλάς).

[ref:Luk 12:42-46|Luke 12:42–46] is the immediate context: the parable of the faithful and unfaithful steward. Verse 47 elaborates on the judgment of the unfaithful servant who knew his master's will.
[ref:Matt 24:45-51|Matthew 24:45–51] is the parallel in Matthew to the parable of the faithful and unfaithful servant, with the same theme of responsibility and judgment.
[ref:Joh 9:41|John 9:41] expresses the same principle: "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, 'We see.' Therefore your sin remains." Knowledge increases responsibility.
[ref:Joh 13:17|John 13:17] says: "Now you know this. Blessed are you if you do it." Knowing the Lord's will obligates one to act.
[ref:Joh 15:22|John 15:22] emphasizes that knowledge of truth removes any excuse for sin: "If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have been without sin."

[ref:Heb 10:26-27|Hebrews 10:26–27] warns that the one who sins willfully after receiving knowledge of the truth has nothing left but a fearful expectation of judgment – the same principle of knowledge and responsibility.

[ref:2 Pet 2:21|2 Peter 2:21] says it would have been better not to have known the way of righteousness than to know it and then turn away – responsibility increases with knowledge of the Lord's will.
